quickfire.question: Which field is required in every singly linked list node declaration?
options: A pointer to the previous node
A pointer to the next node
quickfire.answer: A pointer to the next node

routineWriter.questionText: Write the node declaration (struct) for a singly linked list in C.

commonMistakes.description: next must be a pointer to struct Node — a value type creates infinite recursion
The data field — omitting it is incomplete

quickfire.question: In insertAtEnd, the while-loop condition that walks to the last node is: while (curr->next _____ NULL)

routineWriter.questionText: Write the routine for insertAtEnd in a singly linked list.

commonMistakes.description: Empty-list guard — missing this causes a null-dereference on the traversal
Stop at last node (curr->next is NULL), not at NULL itself
Attach new node — using curr = newNode instead leaves the list unchanged

fullTrace.questionText: Show the step-by-step state after inserting 10, 20, 30 into an initially empty singly linked list.

quickfire.question: When deleting a node from a singly linked list, which pointer must be updated?

routineWriter.questionText: Write the routine for delete (by value) in a singly linked list.

commonMistakes.description: Head-node special case — deleting head requires updating *head itself
Bypass the deleted node by pointing predecessor to successor
Must free — omitting causes a memory leak

quickfire.question: What is the time complexity of finding the k-th node in a singly linked list?

routineWriter.questionText: Write a routine to traverse and print every value in a singly linked list.

commonMistakes.description: Use a separate pointer — never mutate head during traversal
Loop terminates when curr is NULL, not curr->next

quickfire.question: For a headerless singly linked list, is_empty(head) returns true when head _____ NULL.

routineWriter.questionText: Write the routine is_empty for a singly linked list (no header node, head pointer passed directly).

commonMistakes.description: An empty list is simply a NULL head pointer — no traversal needed

quickfire.question: In find, the while-loop condition uses short-circuit _____ so p->element is never read once p is NULL: while (p != NULL && p->value _____ x)

routineWriter.questionText: Write the routine find(head, x) that returns a pointer to the node containing x, or NULL if not found.

commonMistakes.description: p != NULL must come first — && short-circuits so p->value is never dereferenced on a NULL p
Returns NULL naturally when the loop runs off the end — no separate not-found branch needed

quickfire.question: find_previous(head, x) is mainly used to support which other operation?

routineWriter.questionText: Write find_previous(head, x) for a headerless singly linked list: return a pointer to the node whose next field contains x, or NULL if x is the head's value or not found at all.

commonMistakes.line: if (head == NULL || head->value == x) return NULL;
commonMistakes.description: Headerless-list edge case: x at the head has no predecessor node — must return NULL, not head
Look one node ahead (p->next), since we want the node BEFORE the match
Ran off the end without finding x — distinguish this from a real predecessor

quickfire.question: insert_after(p, value) wires the new node's next BEFORE updating p->next. The new node's next is set to: p->_____

routineWriter.questionText: Write insert_after(p, value): insert a new node containing value immediately after position p (p is guaranteed non-NULL).

commonMistakes.description: Must save p->next into the new node FIRST — doing p->next = tmp before this loses the rest of the list
This splice-in step must come after tmp->next is wired, not before
malloc can fail — an unchecked NULL dereference on tmp->value is a common exam deduction

quickfire.question: Why is `while (p != NULL) { free(p); p = p->next; }` wrong for deleting an entire list?
options: p->next is read AFTER p has already been freed — undefined behavior
It only works for circular lists
quickfire.answer: p->next is read AFTER p has already been freed — undefined behavior

routineWriter.questionText: Write delete_list(headPtr): free every node in the list and set *headPtr to NULL. Must be safe (no use-after-free).

commonMistakes.description: Save next BEFORE freeing p — this is the whole point of the routine; skipping it is the classic wrong version (free(p); p = p->next;)
Free only after tmp has safely captured the next pointer
Caller's head pointer must be cleared too, or it dangles
